Great views and a lovely meal.
Nov 2025 • Couples
We have just come back from Shri and we actually had a really lovely time. We walked across the glass bridge from the Hotel Des Art, where we are staying, as we saw the lights from the rooftop bar of our hotel, where we were having a drink (The Social Club). Anyway, we decided to have dinner, as it looked really nice. And it WAS really nice. 
I had a Proscutto, fig and blue cheese starter and a vegetarian cheesy, artichoke pasta main. My husband had grilled scallops and chickpea starter and a Ribeye steak main, with a side of mashed truffle potatoes and asparagus. All were delicious and perfectly cooked.
I have only a couple of constructive criticisms: 
The background music was of that elevator type. It might be what Vietnamese people like, but as the restaurant was pretty empty, if they wanted to try and to lure Western tourists in, the music might be putting them off somewhat.
There are no sides to the menu, apart from some grilled asparagus. We asked for French fries with the steak, and there are none. We were offered mashed potatoes, which was not listed on the menu, which was fine, but a few chips (truffle parmesan or normal) would have been great.
Not that this detracts much; it was a great place with a fantastic view, and I heartily recommend it. Also a special mention to the young male waiter called Kin. He was absolutely great!

Thomas G
Dear mr Lam,

Wine sediment or wine crystal in a wine is common especially for high end wines where the producer choose to not filter the wine as it strips the wine of some of its character. I am surprised you never come across this before and I apologise if this was not explained to you when you were here. I guarantee this does not have any impact on the quality of the wine, and is not harmful. I would say the opposite it shows that the wine is a rather high end wine. The wine you had was a Bordeaux wine from Fronsac and you can often find wine sediment or wine crystal in wine from Bordeaux, next time we will decant the wine for you, this is the best way to avoid the sediment when you pour it.
Wine is a living, breathing beverage like no other and continue develop in the bottle, and the wine sediment/crystal is a proof of that.

I can guarantee it is not the staffs fault, it is actually the wine itself and the producer of the wine who makes it. However I apologise that you felt the way you did and I suggest you read this article which explains a bit more about wine sediment and wine crystals.

https://www.goldmedalwineclub.com/blog/post/the-gritty-truth-why-is-there-sediment-in-my-wine

I hope you continue discover wines and you are more than welcome back to try more wines from our large selection.

All the best

Thomas, General Manager
